inventories.summary: Celnet's quant core is a Rust FX-options pricing stack spanning vanilla Garman-Kohlhagen pricing with a full 14-Greek set, the four FX delta conventions plus a guarded branch-aware strike↔delta solver, ATM/DNS strike rules, a complete smile/surface engine (Vanna-Volga, SABR, raw-SVI, SSVI, broker→smile-strangle calibration, arbitrage-free term structure), and a broad first-generation exotics catalogue (digitals, one-/no-touch, double-no-touch, single/double barriers with Crank-Nicolson+Rannacher PDE and Philox Monte Carlo, plus a survival-weighted Vanna-Volga overlay). Correctness is gated against an independent QuantLib 1.42.1 golden oracle at last-bit-to-near tolerances (vanilla/barrier/digital ~1e-9–1e-11 relative; touch/double-barrier ~1e-6). Most of this cluster is Shipped and gated green per the implementation ledger (G1/G2/G3). The notable In-flight item is the celnet-calendar ON/SN+IMM correction: the committed HEAD still resolves Overnight incorrectly, while the working tree carries the fix (381 added lines, uncommitted) landing via the running Phase 1+2 workflow. Since this digest was first written, the LSV particle-method booking model and Sobol' QMC + Brownian-bridge path construction (celnet-qmc) have BOTH been BUILT and parity-gated; Dupire local-vol stripping ships in celnet-surface.

inventories.cluster: ENGINE, PERFORMANCE, GPU, DURABILITY (celnet-engine, celnet-gpu, celnet-bench, celnet-journal, celnet-core)
inventories.summary: Celnet's hot-core/performance/GPU/durability cluster delivers a two-tier pricing runtime: a non-async, core-pinned, zero-allocation busy-poll pricing core joined to the async edge by wait-free SPSC rings, with lock-free read-mostly state publication (arc-swap whole-MarketState snapshot, single-writer seqlock top-of-book). It is the measured backbone of the §1.2 latency budget: vanilla price + full Greeks in ~23 ns median in-core (~85x inside the 2 µs p50), batched ~105 ns/option (~9.5x the 1M/s/core throughput target), with the wire-path round-trip honestly separated (~388 µs p50 loopback CI-gate, dominated by gRPC/HTTP-2 framing, not pricing). A wgpu/Metal/Vulkan f32 GBM Monte-Carlo backend sits behind a scalar-generic PricingBackend trait with an f64 CPU oracle, a bit-identical counter-based Philox-4x32-10 RNG (Rust ↔ WGSL), and a derived f32↔f64 reconciliation bound. Durability is closed by celnet-journal — a dependency-free fsync'd, CRC-32, sequence-ordered append-only WAL with clean torn-tail truncation — wired into the engine to rebuild book+market state byte-identically at startup, strictly off the hot path. Observability is zero hot-path cost: the core only bumps CachePadded Relaxed counters and pushes POD samples into a bounded drop-on-full SPSC ring; an off-core drain folds them into HdrHistograms (p50/p99/p99.9, coordinated-omission aware). AAD/batched-GPU adjoint Greeks and cross-fleet distributed risk fan-out are honestly deferred (designed-only).

capabilities.name: Zero-allocation core-pinned hot pricing path
capabilities.description: Non-async busy-poll PricingCore pinned to an isolated core (via core_affinity) that turns celnet-vanilla closed-form GK + the full Greek set into price+Greeks with zero heap allocation on the path — all pools pre-sized at construction, no locks, no syscalls, no synchronous logging. PricingCore::run drives the loop with a race-free shutdown doing a final lossless drain. Proven, not asserted: tests/zero_alloc.rs (hot_pricing_loop_allocates_zero) asserts zero heap allocations under a counting global allocator, with a deliberate-alloc negative control.

capabilities.name: Wait-free SPSC core↔edge rings (rtrb)
capabilities.description: RequestRing/ResponseRing over rtrb carry Copy/POD request and response records edge→core and core→edge; RING_CAPACITY = 1<<12, power-of-two so index arithmetic is a mask not a modulo. A full ring surfaces back-pressure to the caller rather than allocating. This is the only join between the async edge and the pinned core — never locks or unbounded channels.

capabilities.name: Lock-free read-mostly state publication (arc-swap MarketState + seqlock top-of-book)
capabilities.description: StateHandle publishes the whole live MarketState (calibrated smile, spot, both rates, vol-time, resolved ConventionRecord) atomically via arc-swap; the hot read path uses a cached StateReader that deliberately avoids arc-swap's allocating load guard so it stays alloc-free even under concurrent publishers (proven by hot_pricing_under_concurrent_publish_allocates_zero). A single-writer Seqlock publishes small Copy PriceSnapshots to many readers with per-word atomic copies (readers retry on torn read) so reader/writer overlap is never a data race. PaddedCounter wraps hot atomics in CachePadded to kill false sharing.

capabilities.name: Blue-green live-state handoff codec

capabilities.name: Durable crash-recovery journal (fsync'd CRC-32 WAL)
capabilities.description: celnet-journal: dependency-free, fsync'd, append-only, sequence-ordered log. Each record is payload_len(u32 LE)|sequence(u64 LE)|payload|crc32(u32 LE) with an IEEE CRC-32 over header+payload. append() returns only after File::sync_data flushes to stable storage (and open() fsyncs the parent directory once for first-creation durability). On open a torn tail (truncated final frame or CRC fail on last record) heals to the last good record and truncates; a CRC-valid but non-monotonic-sequence interior record is surfaced as JournalError::CorruptInterior rather than healed. MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN guards the recovery allocation. Wired into celnet-engine::journal: DurableBook fsyncs each booked line/accepted mark via the SHARED handoff byte codec (write_book_entry/read_book_entry — no format fork), and recover() replays at startup to rebuild BookState+MarketState that reprices bit-identically. Strictly off the hot path (pricing_a_journalled_book_allocates_zero proves price() never touches the journal).

capabilities.name: Bit-stable counter-based Philox-4×32-10 RNG (Rust ↔ WGSL) + f32↔f64 reconciliation
capabilities.description: Philox-4×32-10 counter-based stateless RNG seeded by (global_seed, path, step, dim), perfectly parallel and order-independent. The same ten-round transform is implemented byte-for-byte in Rust (counter_rng.rs) and WGSL (shader.wgsl), sharing constants so the 32-bit integer output is bit-identical on CPU and GPU; only int→float conversion (f64 CPU vs f32 GPU) and payoff arithmetic differ. Payoff accumulation uses integer/tree reduction (no float atomics — WGSL atomics are integer-only) so reduction order is fixed and reproducible. A derived (not asserted) f32-vs-f64 error bound on the mean discounted price gates GPU↔CPU↔closed-form agreement (gpu_reconciles_with_cpu_and_closed_form). All CPU transcendentals route through celnet_core::math (rust-lang/libm) for cross-OS/arch bit-identity.

Audit (quote/trade lifecycle) is a SEPARATE lossless, back-pressured, fsync'd ring that never drops a booking event.

inventories.summary: Celnet's risk layer splits cleanly into shipped single-instrument/book-shaped risk and an in-flight firm-wide aggregation tier. Shipped today: per-instrument book-shaped risk computed by the server scenario service (transport.scenario / RiskBucketRequest -> BucketedRisk) — bucketed vega per (tenor, delta) pillar, a cross-gamma 2-D stencil per factor-pair, and a theta-roll over requested horizons — plus the versioned marked-surface registry (SurfaceBook / surface_version pinning) and a shipped GUI Book->Risk drill with a labelled TrendMode. The firm-wide OLAP risk cube is now landing in-flight as four new crates (celnet-risk-normalize -> celnet-risk-cube -> celnet-limits || celnet-entitlements): the position-fact cube over an immutable RiskFact table, convention canonicalization + common-numeraire netting, additive incremental roll-up vs per-node re-derivation of non-additive measures (historical VaR/ES, SbM curvature, correlation-weighted vega), a cascading limit tree with pre/post-trade checks, and server-side entitlement pruning. These crates compile and pass 39 unit tests but are uncommitted (untracked) and not yet wired into celnet-server/-proto/-client, so they are In-flight rather than Shipped. Two pieces are honestly deferred: AAD / batched-GPU adjoint Greeks for non-additive reval (RISK-HIERARCHY §3.3 — present only as bump-and-revalue today), and cross-fleet distributed risk fan-out (celnet-router is designed-only).

inventories.summary: Celnet ships a frozen, single-version, runtime-agnostic user-extensibility SDK contract (celnet-plugin-api) and a Shipped tiered execution host (celnet-plugin-host) that lets quants run custom vol-smile models, vanilla pricers, and calibrators in-engine while keeping their IP private. The contract is three POD-in/POD-out trait seams — PricingModel, SmileModel (extends celnet_core::Smile, with a built-in butterfly-arbitrage self-check), and Calibration — plus a self-describing ModelDescriptor/ModelRegistry so the engine routes work by purpose without knowing a model's concrete type or tier. A WIT world (wit/celnet.wit) structurally mirrors the Rust traits one-to-one. The host runs first-party models native (Tier-0, hot path, zero ABI/sandbox cost) and untrusted user models on a wasmi 1.0.9 pure-Rust, fuel-metered, no-WASI sandbox (Tier-2) whose only granted authority is the libm transcendentals of celnet_core::math; both tiers present one tier-blind HostModel handle behind one unified ModelRegistry, so native and Wasm models are interchangeable. Determinism is a contract obligation enforced by a replay harness (bit-identity across runs) and boundary NaN-canonicalization, with a per-call fuel budget as the compute SLA (exhaustion is a typed HostError, never a hang). Tier-1 (stabby-loaded signed .so for trusted partners) and Tier-3 (Linux Landlock+seccomp outer ring) are Designed-only in PLUGIN-HOST-ALT.md.

Uses only celnet_core::math (deterministic, cross-platform); a model arb-free by construction can override with a cheaper proof. The host can run this during replay before admitting a user surface to the hot path.

capabilities.name: Host-controlled (ptr,len) core-module ABI + boundary NaN-canonicalization
capabilities.description: The host owns the calling convention end-to-end onto core Wasm (no Component Model needed): VanillaInputs marshals as 6 little-endian f64s into a guest scratch buffer (celnet_scratch_in), Greeks read back as 14 little-endian f64s (celnet_scratch_out), price returned in a register, option type as an i32 discriminant (0=Call,1=Put with out-of-range rejected). Every f64 crossing the boundary in both directions is NaN-canonicalized to one canonical quiet-NaN bit pattern (0x7ff8...) so a guest cannot smuggle a non-canonical NaN payload into a replay. Guest memory access is bounds-checked by wasmi; a negative/out-of-range ptr surfaces as HostError::AbiViolation. A guest can signal a domain rejection via negative status codes mapped back to PluginError so a Tier-2 rejection is indistinguishable from a Tier-0 one.

capabilities.name: Per-call fuel budget as deterministic compute SLA
capabilities.description: FuelBudget (default 50,000,000) is wasmi's deterministic instruction-cost counter (R1-compatible, unlike wall-clock interruption); fuel is reset before every guest call so each gets the full SLA and fuel accounting is part of the replay invariant. Exhaustion interrupts the interpreter at the budget and yields a typed HostError::FuelExhausted — never a hang or panic. The store is also fueled before instantiation so a runaway module (start) function is fuel-bounded at load, not just at call. Resource budgets (64 MiB linear memory, 4096 table elements, 1 memory/table/instance) are enforced in-engine via a StoreLimits ResourceLimiter with trap_on_grow_failure, so an over-budget grow traps as HostError::ResourceLimit and a hostile guest can never OOM/hang the host.

It implements the frozen celnet_plugin_api::ModelRegistry discovery trait (descriptor/provides/of_kind) so it plugs into the engine without a bespoke discovery path. Each handle is single-threaded (owns its own wasmi Store reset per call), matching how the engine fans an IB-sized portfolio across workers each with its own handle.

capabilities.name: Deterministic replay / bit-identity harness (R1 proof)
capabilities.description: A replay harness replays a fixed market snapshot through a HostModel N times and asserts every output f64 (price + all 14 Greeks) is to_bits-equal across runs — proving identical inputs ⇒ bit-identical output, including canonicalized NaN. assert_agree proves two independently-loaded models (e.g. a native Tier-0 and Wasm Tier-2 twin sharing op-order + the same libm) price a snapshot to the last bit. The crate documents honestly that bit-identity between an arbitrary Tier-0 and Tier-2 pair is NOT automatic — it holds only when both perform the same IEEE-754 op sequence through the same rust-lang/libm; otherwise agreement is within the model's documented tolerance and a tolerance comparator is the right gate.

methodologies: Static (butterfly) no-arbitrage check via risk-neutral density positivity: undiscounted Black call C(K)=F·Φ(d1)−K·Φ(d2) evaluated per-strike with that strike's own smile vol, asserting the strike second-difference C(K-)−2C(K)+C(K+) ≥ 0 — a direct, model-free density-positivity test (call-spread / butterfly no-arbitrage conditions; provenance in doc comment only, per guardrail 8)

Deterministic-replay bit-identity testing: replay a fixed market snapshot N times and assert every output f64 is to_bits-equal (not ==), so two canonicalized NaNs compare equal and ±0.0 compare unequal — the exact reproducibility notion the sandbox must enforce

Boundary NaN canonicalization: collapse any NaN payload to one canonical quiet-NaN bit pattern (0x7ff8000000000000) on every f64 crossing the host↔guest boundary, removing Wasm's multi-NaN-payload degree of freedom

Deterministic instruction-cost (fuel) metering as the compute SLA instead of wall-clock interruption, so the same module + same fuel interrupts at the same instruction on every platform (R1-compatible)
Capability-based security: zero ambient authority via an explicit allow-listed host-import surface (only libm transcendentals), no WASI linked, with a pre-link import audit

Finite-difference validation of the full 14-Greek set (delta/vega/theta/rho via central difference of price; gamma/vanna/volga/charm/speed/zomma/color via central difference of the relevant first-order Greek) across multiple market regimes as the correctness gate for any conforming model
performance_numbers: Default per-call fuel budget = 50,000,000 instruction-cost units (FuelBudget::DEFAULT, wasm.rs) — sized for per-quote (not per-tick) model evaluation

Tier-2 wasmi interpreter is ~10×–50× slower than a JIT (PLUGIN-HOST-ALT.md §3.1/§7) — accepted by design because untrusted Wasm is reserved for non-per-tick models while Tier-0 native carries the hot path; honest design trade-off, not a measured Celnet latency number
Tier-2 resource caps: 64 MiB (1024 pages) max guest linear memory, 4096 max table elements, 1 memory / 1 table / 1 instance (host.rs) — hard ceilings enforced in-engine
caveats: Tier-1 (stabby signed-.so trusted-partner) and Tier-3 (Linux Landlock+seccomp outer ring) are Designed-only in docs/PLUGIN-HOST-ALT.md and explicitly 'designed, not yet wired' per the CLAUDE.md ledger — not Shipped.

Bit-identity between an arbitrary Tier-0 native model and a Tier-2 Wasm model is NOT a general guarantee: the crate's own lib.rs and replay.rs document that it holds only when both perform the same IEEE-754 op sequence through the same rust-lang/libm; otherwise agreement is within the model's documented numerical tolerance, and the bit-exact assert_agree is the wrong gate (use a tolerance comparator). The strong bit-identity claim is proven only for a deliberately op-order-matched twin pair in tests/sandbox.rs.

wasmi hosts core Wasm modules, not the Component Model (wasmi's CM is WIP), so the host hand-rolls the WIT→core-module (ptr,len) ABI lowering; the WIT world is a frozen spec/doc mirror, not generated component bindings.

The granted capability surface is intentionally minimal (5 libm math functions, no market-data lookups wired) — the design document mentions market-data lookups as a possible host-import but only the celnet_core::math primitives are actually granted in host.rs::GRANTED_IMPORTS.

inventories.cluster: EDGE, API CONTRACT, WIRE, INTEGRATION FABRIC
inventories.summary: Celnet's edge tier exposes one clean, unversioned wire contract (`celnet-proto`, ADR-0007: no schema_version, no N/N-1 shims) as a tonic gRPC server plus a byte-identical WebSocket JSON mirror, both dispatching onto the same async edge over wait-free SPSC rings to the pinned hot core. The contract spans five service families — PricingService (one-shot 14-Greek pricing), QuoteService (RFQ request/accept/reject with idempotency + last-look), StreamService (one multiplexed bidirectional StreamSession carrying many subscriptions with per-sub seq/snapshot/delta/heartbeat/resync, in-place Modify, and click-to-trade Execute by cryptographically-unforgeable keyed-MAC token), and SurfaceService (GetSmile/MarkSurface/Scenario) — with surface_version pinning threaded through every priced path so a quote is reproducibly tied to a specific mark. API-first client parity is the governing rule: the typed `celnet-client` SDK, the WS mirror, the admin CLI, and Excel all consume this single contract. Integration fabric ships as a real hand-rolled FIX 4.4 acceptor+initiator (`celnet-fix`), a vendor-feed ingest→normalize→blend pipeline with a deployment-mode seam and a bounded conflating egress governor (`celnet-integration`), and a designed-only fleet router (`celnet-router`). Currently in-flight via the Phase 1+2 workflow: contract extensions for a SmileModel selector, a market-series feed, and an attribution identity, plus server wiring and four new risk crates.

inventories.summary: Celnet's competitive position is anchored by an executable parity matrix: the crate `celnet-parity` renders 15 capability claims-vs-incumbents as gated integration tests (`tests/{conventions,greeks,surface,broker_smile,exotics,determinism}.rs`) that reprice reference inputs, check convention/arbitrage invariants, and demonstrate features incumbents treat as opaque — so "meets or beats SynOption/Fenics/Bloomberg/Murex" is continuously proven, not asserted. On the axes that are built and tested, Celnet out-functions (user-selectable arbitrage-free smile models, particle-calibrated LSV, GPU Monte-Carlo as a live service, an open quant SDK runtime), out-intuits (convention transparency on every message, auditable arb report, broker→smile exact reprice), and out-performs (published, reproducible microsecond latency + blue-green zero-downtime upgrades) — a combination no single incumbent offers. The GA verdict is GO for the pricing platform, with the latency-under-load gating caveat now MET per the GA-READINESS rev-3 header. Honest deferrals remain: structured-product breadth, asset-class/pair breadth (~9 G10 + few EM NDFs vs incumbents' 75–300+), GPU perf-on-real-NVIDIA, live Celer/FIX wiring, and cross-fleet distributed risk fan-out.
